title: Perfect Days is a portrayal of tamed melancholy

commenti.body: I think your writing describes it much better than your title. It’s more like he has “enlightened monotony”. Most of us would die in three days if we had this man’s life but he is able to find joy in taking the same pictures of trees, drinking the same coffee, and cleaning toilets. He listens to our old music and reads our old books. It is almost as if Hirayama lives off the scraps of life that we ignore, he takes the things we don’t appreciate and gives them all the care in the world. How the surrounding characters seem stressed, desire his tapes, and pity him are the reasons he lives this life and the reason he actually feels sorry for them. His niece, the lady having lunch and the homeless man in the park being the only people who really see him for the remarkable person he is.
